object_types.name: Vendor
object_types.definition: A supplier from which the organization procures goods or services, identified by a unique vendor number.

source_references.excerpt: The vendor record. It's the thing in the supplier master... Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.
Every vendor has exactly one, and no two vendors share one?... Yes. That one I'm sure about. It's the thing we quote in every conversation with AP.

object_types.name: VendorNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier assigned to each vendor upon record creation.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.

object_types.name: LegalName
object_types.definition: The official legal name of the vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Legal name. Tax ID. Address...

object_types.name: TaxID
object_types.definition: The tax identification number of the vendor, not unique due to duplicate entities and parent-subsidiary structures.

source_references.excerpt: Legal name. Tax ID. Address...
We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The operational status of a vendor record.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended... It defaults to draft the moment the record is created.
Collapsed into three, yes. Draft, active, suspended. That's what the field allows now. Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: A tier classification based on spending volume with the vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold.
I'm talking about spend. Gold vendors are the ones we spend real money with, they get quarterly business reviews, better payment terms, a named relationship manager.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: A tier classification based on risk assessment determined by the vendor's risk review.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high.
And I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

object_types.name: Address
object_types.definition: A physical address associated with a vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A compliance review record for a vendor that must be completed and signed off before the vendor can be moved to active status.

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review. Not zero, and the one has to be signed off.
The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: ReviewId
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a risk review record.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: Region

source_references.excerpt: It's the combination of the vendor and the region that determines the contact... A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.

ambiguities.description: Address granularity: The transcript mentions three distinct address types (remit-to, ship-from, legal), but the model currently captures 'Address' as a single value type without distinguishing between these types. Should Address be decomposed into specific address types, or should the model include an AddressType value type with a ternary relationship 'Vendor has Address of AddressType'?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Vendor status and in-flight orders: The transcript explicitly states that what happens to purchase orders when a vendor transitions from active to suspended is undecided policy, not a modeling concern. The model currently captures only that the status field has three values. Should the model include constraints about the relationship between Vendor status and PurchaseOrder, or does that remain parked pending policy decision?

source_references.excerpt: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided... That's a fair statement of it.

ambiguities.description: Current risk review identification: The transcript discusses that a vendor can have multiple risk reviews over time, but exactly one must be 'current' and 'signed off' to make the vendor active. The model currently only captures that a review has a ReviewId and concerns exactly one vendor. Should there be explicit attributes on the RiskReview entity to mark it as 'current' and 'signed off', or constraints that model this state?

source_references.excerpt: But one of them is the current signed-off one... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor contact optionality: The transcript states 'If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.' This implies that a vendor does not necessarily have a contact for every region. The ternary relationship 'Vendor operates in Region with Contact' captures the combination, but the rule 'if they don't operate in a region, there's no contact' is not formally stated as a constraint. Is contact optional per region, or should this be explicitly mandatory only for regions where the vendor operates?

source_references.excerpt: And can a vendor have no contact in a region?... If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all. Most of our vendors are one region only. It's the big ones that are multi-region.

ambiguities.description: Risk tier assignment mechanism: The transcript indicates that RiskTier is derived from or determined by the RiskReview, but the model does not capture which specific review record (if a vendor has multiple accumulated reviews) determines the current risk tier. Is the risk tier always synchronized with the 'current' review mentioned in the policy, or could there be edge cases?

source_references.excerpt: A vendor with no review has no risk tier.
And I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

ambiguities.description: PurchaseOrder creation control: The transcript states that you cannot create a PO against a vendor who isn't active, implying a control at creation time. Should there be an explicit constraint 'PurchaseOrder can only be raised against an active Vendor', or is this a system-level control that does not need to be modeled as a formal constraint?

source_references.excerpt: A PO is raised against exactly one vendor, and you can't raise one against a vendor who isn't active.

ambiguities.description: Contact name, email, and phone optionality: The transcript mentions that a contact has 'name, email, phone number', but does not explicitly state whether each of these is mandatory or optional. Should all three properties of a contact be required, or are some optional?

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.

ambiguities.description: Region code enumeration: The transcript lists four regions (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM) and notes 'There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.' Should the value_constraint on RegionCode reflect only the current four values, or note the potential for future expansion?

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM... Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Spend tier default: The transcript states that bronze is the default if a vendor hasn't been assessed, and every vendor gets a spend tier. Does 'getting a spend tier' mean it is automatically assigned upon record creation, or is there a distinction between draft vendors that default to bronze and others that receive assessment later?

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor gets a spend tier. Bronze by default if nobody's assessed them.

ambiguities.description: TaxID non-uniqueness: The transcript explicitly states that TaxID is not unique due to parent-subsidiary structures and duplicate record creation. The model captures this in the definition and source references, but should there be an explicit constraint noting that TaxID is NOT an identifier (e.g., an exclusion or negation constraint)?

source_references.excerpt: Could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?... You'd think so, but no... Tax ID isn't an identifier, vendor number is.
